subject.title: feat(workspace): add tiered bootstrap loading with configurable bootstrapTier

question: Should OpenClaw accept `agents.defaults.bootstrapTier` now, and should unset config preserve legacy filtering while explicit tiers use this PR's `minimal`/`standard`/`full` semantics?
rationale: The implementation is bounded, but a new config/default surface changes prompt context and session state semantics across bootstrap files and hook-loaded extras, which automation should not decide without maintainer intent.

options.title: Sponsor the bounded PR shape
options.body: Accept the new default-level config surface after correcting the unset-vs-explicit tier contract text, adding public docs, refreshing the branch, and keeping no-override behavior unchanged.

options.title: Fold into broader bootstrap selection
options.body: Pause this PR behind the broader bootstrap/context-selection design so tiering, dynamic loading, and prompt-pressure work share one public contract.

options.title: Decline the new config knob
options.body: Keep existing fixed filters and steer users toward current context budgets, `contextInjection`, lightweight modes, and docs instead of adding `bootstrapTier`.

recommendation.title: Sponsor the bounded PR shape
recommendation.body: Accept the new default-level config surface after correcting the unset-vs-explicit tier contract text, adding public docs, refreshing the branch, and keeping no-override behavior unchanged.

likelyOwner.reason: The subagent bootstrap filtering history and prior review context make this the best available owner for the product/API decision.
